item.title: After years of poking fun at Green Lantern, Ryan Reynolds admitted he owes his career and personal life to the infamous 2011 DC superhero movie.
item.description: Ryan Reynolds has spent over a decade mocking his notorious 2011 comic book movie flop, Green Lantern, perhaps most famously by including a meta post-credits scene in Deadpool 2 where the merc with a mouth goes back in time to blow out Reynolds’ brains all over a copy of the Green Lantern screenplay. Now, with the HBO series Lanterns out, the actor seems to have developed an appreciation for his DC film, declaring, “I owe my entire career to that movie.” Speaking on the red carpet at the premiere of his new movie Mayday, Reynolds was asked by Entertainment Tonight if he’d ever consider making a cameo in Lanterns. "I would totally do a cameo in that," Reynolds said. "I love it. I learned so much making that movie. And I know what you're thinking, you're thinking, 'Oh, learned what not to do.' In part, yes. But also, any time you're making something that large, there are core lessons that come of it.” “I owe my entire career to that movie. I owe everything to that,” Reynolds said. “Everything about it was a gift that keeps on giving. And I really enjoyed the experience of making it."

item.title: Takashi Iizuka, a key figure in Sega’s Sonic Franchise, told IGN’s Jeffrey Vega about the unique difficulty the company faced in giving the Blue Blur a playable skin in Fortnite.
item.description: Takashi Iizuka, a key figure in Sega’s Sonic Franchise, told IGN’s Jeffrey Vega about the unique difficulty the company faced in giving the Blue Blur a playable skin in Fortnite. While Shadow is somewhat famous for being an edgy, pistol-toting anti-hero, Sonic is a totally different character. The yang to Shadow’s yin, Sonic is an upbeat hedgehog who uses his extremely fast speed (and occasionally, the power of the Chaos Emeralds) to take down enemies. That’s why Sega balked when it was first approached by Epic games with the idea of giving Shadow and Sonic their own Fortnite skins, according to Sonic Creative Officer Takashi Iizuka. Luckily, they were able to come up with a creative solution: Why not make a new Sonic variant? “Epic Games came and spoke with us a couple years ago about putting Sonic in Fortnite, but Sonic is a character that will never hold a gun,” he told us. “And when thinking about the design of Fortnite, it was really hard to think about Sonic being in the game. But this time, we were able to take creative liberties and created Android Sonic.”

item.title: A former Rockstar Games developer has revealed that the team thought GTA Online was going to fail before it launched.
item.description: A former Rockstar Games developer has revealed that the team thought GTA Online was going to fail before it launched. In an interview with Eldorado, ex-Rockstar Games developer Matt Freedman looked back on the success of GTA 5 and attributed a lot of it to GTA Online. He noted that a lot of investors seek a GTA Online-level success nowadays, but said it was treated as an "afterthought" during its initial development. "When we were working on GTA Online, it was an afterthought," said Freedman. "We were all positive it was going to fail. Everyone thought this thing was going to fail. I remember QA testers coming up to me [and saying], 'We’ve got four hours of content for online mode. To do everything in GTA Online, it’s four hours,' or it was something like that. It was really short, and they’re like: ‘We are in so much trouble,' and we’re all sitting there going, 'Let’s see what happens. We’re going to do our best job anyways.' And then it took off, and then there was, to Rockstar’s credit, a fast follow with as much content as possible and [it] just kind of keep it going. And now it’s become this phenomenon." It's unclear when the perception of GTA Online's potential began to shift at Rockstar. The studio did seem to have ambitions for it before launch, as it released a sizable trailer and media previews for the online mode before the game's release with plans for post-launch content like heists. Still, Freedman is right that the game was pretty light on content upon arrival. There wasn't a ton to do beyond the typical sandbox mayhem and the most exciting content in the game didn't arrive until years later, including its heists update.

item.title: Sony's State of Play for September 2026 has now concluded without any sign of Naughty Dog's upcoming Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, as well as many other first-party PlayStation games that fans had hoped to see.
item.description: Sony's State of Play for September 2026 has now concluded without any sign of Naughty Dog's upcoming Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, as well as many other first-party PlayStation games that fans had hoped to see. The showcase was notable for its string of other no-shows, including further updates on God of War: Laufey, Horizon Hunters Gathering, Fairgames, and any kind of update for what will happen to Bungie's Marathon. The wait also continues for more news on what several other PlayStation Studios are working on, including Dreams maker Media Molecule and Days Gone studio Sony Bend. It has now been six years since Media Molecule last shipped a game, and seven since Bend first launched Days Gone. Ahead of the showcase, hopes were high that Naughty Dog would bring the curtain down on today's proceedings, particularly as the studio broke its relative radio silence this week to confirm that it had now completed Intergalactic's performance capture. In hindsight, this confirmation now feels more like an acknowledgement that no other update would be provided today, with word that the project was progresing simply provided instead. Naughty Dog last shipped an all-new game in 2020, with The Last of Us 2, though has spent time since on various remakes, and its now-scrapped multiplayer The Last of Us spinoff.

item.title: The addition of three new anime-inspired game has brought Crunchyroll's Game Vault into the triple digits.
item.description: Crunchyroll’s Game Vault has officially crossed over 100 games. The Game Vault originally launched back in 2023 with a limited number of titles, largely connected to various anime series and properties. The recent addition of three new games has brought the vault's total to 101, and now Crunchyroll is offering a look at what’s next for the anime-themed gaming service. The Game Vault is exclusive to Mega and Ultimate Fan subscribers, who also get access to the service’s anime streaming library, the Crunchyroll Store, and the recently launched Crunchyroll Manga service. You can check out the full Game Vault library here. The Crunchyroll Game Vault recently launched three new games that brought its full catalog into the triple digits. All of these games are playable on mobile with touch screen controls or through a browser, where you can use a mouse and keyboard or connect your own PC-compatible controller.

item.title: Fallout, the blockbuster Bethesda Game Studios RPG and hit Prime Video show, is now also a pinball game, courtesy of Stern Pinball. The Pro Edition, Premium Edition, and Limited Edition are available now for $7,299 (Pro), $10,699 (Premium), and $13,999 (Limited). The Limited Edition is capped at 770 games globally as a nod to Fallout's Great War of 2077.
item.description: Fallout, the blockbuster Bethesda Game Studios RPG and hit Prime Video show, is now also a pinball game, courtesy of Stern Pinball. The Pro Edition, Premium Edition, and Limited Edition are available now for $7,299 (Pro), $10,699 (Premium), and $13,999 (Limited). The decked-out Limited Edition is capped at 770 games globally as a nod to Fallout's Great War of 2077. Three characters are available: Lucy MacLean, The Ghoul, or Maximus. An on-table Pip-Boy provides game mode information and features and can be used in-game to hack computer terminals. The playfield also includes other classic Fallout features like Vault Boy, Power Armor, Nuka-Cola, Pip-Boy, and Vault suits. Meanwhile, Stern notes, "The Fat Man multi-axis pinball launcher with Vault-Tec Assisted Targeting System (V.A.T.S), a combat mechanic inspired by the video game, launches balls to an upper playfield target gallery. The Nuka-Cola Bottle Cap spinner exhibits first-of-its-kind mechanical up and down movement, while the ‘Mutated’ inverted upper flipper delivers mechanical innovation not seen in pinball since before the Great War. Additional features include the Mechanical Vault Blast Door that opens and allows players to explore underground unknowns, a Deathclaw bash toy with kickback and taunt features, and a Vault lower playfield powered by “Magna-Flip” magnetic technology, that provides dynamic kinetic action and excitement." Players can level up their S.P.E.C.I.A.L. to level 10, after which exclusive new game modes for each of the three characters get unlocked. And players are able to carry progress over from game to game using Stern's Insider Connected platform. Stern also says that to "further [celebrate] the iconic IP, the machines seamlessly incorporate footage from throughout seasons 1 and 2 of the TV series and content pulled directly from the Fallout video game series, along with custom callouts from renowned actor Johnny Pemberton, who plays Thaddeus." We thought the Fallout TV show's second season finale was great, and apparently enough viewers agreed, because Amazon renewed the show for a third season, in which Breaking Bad's Aaron Paul will join the cast, as will Star Wars and The Good Place actor Manny Jacinto. So far, the only other thing we know is that season 3 will take place in a new location.

item.title: Rockstar Games and PlayStation have revealed a pair of GTA 6-themed PS5 controllers.
item.description: Rockstar Games and PlayStation have revealed a pair of GTA 6-themed PS5 controllers. During the PlayStation State of Play, we got some unexpected GTA 6 news. PlayStation and Rockstar Games' marketing deal will give birth to two limited edition GTA 6 controllers. One will come in white, the other in black, but both feature the same core design: the VI logo engraved on the touchpad with palm tree etchings around the controller grips. The Grand Theft Auto logo is also etched into the back of the controllers and are rounded out with a sleek, neon purple trim around the bottom half of the controllers. Pre-orders will open for the controllers through PlayStation Direct on September 10, but fans won't be able to get their hands on them until the game's release on November 19. The controllers will set fans back a whopping $84.99 and you should probably anticipate them selling out quickly given the rabid demand for the game. The news comes as GTA 6's marketing begins to really ramp up. Last week, Rockstar debuted the first gameplay for GTA 6 and invited select media (including IGN) to participate in previews for the game. Fans have been suffering for years due to Rockstar's extended gaps of silence, but all of that appears to be coming to an end as GTA 6 has locked in its November release date.

item.title: Square Enix has announced a release date for Final Fantasy 7: Revelation, concluding its acclaimed remake trilogy.
item.description: Square Enix has announced a release date for Final Fantasy 7: Revelation, concluding its acclaimed remake trilogy. The third and final chapter in its Final Fantasy 7 remake saga will arrive on April 8, 2027, it was confirmed today. That date arrived during Sony's latest PlayStation State of Play broadcast and just mentioned the title's PS5 arrival — though we know the game will launch simultaneously for all platforms, meaning this is when you should also expect its Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox Series X/S versions, as well as its PC launch via Steam and the Epic Games Store. Following that, two expansions will also be released over the following 12 months. Story DLC 1: Sephiroth and Story DLC 2: Vincent & the Turks are mentioned as part of a Story Expansion pass that's now visible on Steam. No pricing is available yet for this pass, and no further detail on the story content of these DLCs is mentioned, though this confirms that suggested further chapters are on the way — something fans have expected since the pass previously leaked via the Epic Games Store. All of the game's cast — Cid, Yuffie, Red XIII, Vincent, Barret, Tifa, Cait Sith, and Cloud — made an appearance, with further battle customization detailed. Sidequests will also now play out different depending who you're controlling and, somewhat weirdly, you can skip through dialogue at double speed, making characters sound a bit like chipmunks.

item.title: Until Dawn 2 will release on PS5 this January, as confirmed by a new trailer for the game.
item.description: Until Dawn 2 will release on PS5 this January, as confirmed by a new trailer for the game. During today's PlayStation State of Play, Firesprite showed off a new look at Until Dawn 2, a game that was formally announced this summer. The trailer teases the franchise's signature branching narrative with deadly choices that can radically change the fate of your characters. However, the biggest takeaway is that the game is coming out very soon, much sooner than some of us could have expected. Until Dawn 2 will release on January 28, 2027 with pre-orders opening on September 10. Pre-orders will get access to an "Until Dawn classic" outfit, Akishima Island holiday outfit, and collectible Dr. Hill bobble heads to find throughout the game. There will also be a deluxe edition, which adds Y2K-inspired outfits for all characters and a Diaramoa of Death which lets players "relive every grisly demise with vignettes exploring unique angles of each fatal outcome." PlayStation's 2027 line up is already looking pretty strong, as Until Dawn 2 will release in January and less than a month later, God of War Laufey will make its debut on PS5. There is also a flurry of speculation and rumors that Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet will release in the second half of 2027, which could make it one of PS5's best years to date. We'll just have to wait and see what happens, but next year is going to be an exciting time for gamers.

item.title: Crimson Desert's first expansion releases in October, and it's going to have a ton of game-changing content, including underwater gameplay.
item.description: Crimson Desert's first expansion releases in October, and it's going to have a ton of game-changing content, including underwater gameplay. During today's PlayStation State of Play, Pearl Abyss announced Crimson Desert: Chartering the Unknown, a brand new expansion for one of 2026's breakout titles. The new DLC will release on October 15 and add city building mechanics, underwater exploration, a ship that players can captain, and much more. The DLC takes place after the main story and continues the story of the game, so players should probably go back and finish the game if they haven't already to prepare for the new DLC. As of right now, we're not sure how much this expansion will cost, but it certainly won't be free. Those who pre-order will get a free deep sea diver outfit as a nice bonus. If you were already feeling overwhelmed by all the games coming out in September and October, Pearl Abyss is ensuring you'll have something else to sink dozens of hours into. Crimson Desert debuted earlier this year and immediately became one of the biggest games of 2026. Players were fond off the game's deep open-world RPG mechanics, allowing for nuanced and rich combat and exploration. It's a game that you can sink countless hours into without getting bored, so it's great to see Pearl Abyss is keeping players well-fed so soon after release.

Double Fine has wasted no time in bringing its curious adventure game Keeper to PlayStation 5, just weeks after the studio was ditched by Xbox. Keeper is a colorful and dreamy adventure starring a crumbling lighthouse and a mysterious bird. Despite being critically praised, the project failed to find a wide audience on Xbox Series X/S and PC where it debuted last year, and was Double Fine's penultimate project before Microsoft decided to cut ties with the company. Its arrival on PlayStation isn't a huge surprise — Double Fine has brought other titles to PS5 as well during its now-concluded era of Xbox ownership — though its swift arrival is still notable. Likewise, the fact that this news was confirmed today in Sony's big State of Play broadcast — it's harder to imagine the news appearing in this way had the studio remained under Xbox's thumb. "Exploring Keeper’s surreal world is a feast for the senses, with every detail from its propulsive score to its Seussian flora and fauna pulling me deeper into its tale," we wrote in IGN's Keeper review, awarding it a 9/10 score.

item.title: PlayStation blockbuster Ghost of Yotei is getting a new single-player roguelike mode, Most Wanted, as part of its Complete Edition that includes upcoming expansion Echoes of Sekigahara.
item.description: PlayStation blockbuster Ghost of Yōtei is getting a new single-player roguelike mode, Most Wanted, as part of its Complete Edition that includes its upcoming expansion Echoes of Sekigahara. Take down Most Wanted targets within the mode and you'll progress through tougher fights using various modifiers, and ultimately unlock more characters — including Ghost of Tsushima's Jin Sakai, who arrives with all four of his signature stances. As well as Atsu, Oyuki and Nagato will also be playable, before you unlock Jin. "For Jin, our animation and character art teams worked hard to take his Ghost of Tsushima model and keep it faithful while also applying upgrades for Ghost of Yōtei," wrote Sucker Punch Productions' Andrew Goldfarb. "Jin can use his katana with all four of the original stances from Ghost of Tsushima, helping to exploit enemy weaknesses. He also starts with a Sticky Bomb and hankyu.

item.title: Ryan Reynolds has promised that Marvel will reveal the truth behind Deadpool & Wolverine's mysterious flashforward with Thor — eventually, at least.
item.description: Ryan Reynolds has promised that Marvel will reveal the truth behind that mysterious Deadpool & Wolverine flashforward featuring Thor — eventually, at least. Interviewed by Entertainment Today, Reynolds was asked about the curious moment in his hugely successful Wolverine team-up movie where Deadpool appears to glimpse a future version of himself lying gravely injured, while Chris Hemsworth's Thor looks tearfully on. "Don't we all want to know why was Thor crying? I want to know too," Reynolds teased. "We will find out at some point. And I'm excited for people to find out." Could the moment be coming in Avengers: Doomsday or Avengers: Secret Wars? Here, Reynolds appeared to plead complete ignorance of his potential role in either film, despite having appeared at both San Diego Comic-Con and D23 this summer to help promote the movie.

item.title: Destiny fans are spamming Sony’s State of Play livestream chat with the hashtag #WeWantDestiny, as they continue to call for more from Bungie’s looter shooter franchise, including Destiny 3.
item.description: Destiny fans are spamming Sony’s State of Play livestream chat with the hashtag #WeWantDestiny, as they continue to call for more from Bungie’s looter shooter franchise, including Destiny 3. At the time of this article’s publication, with 15 minutes until today’s State of Play (check out our live blog here for all the announcements), chat across various livestreams was packed with #WeWantDestiny as well as calls for Destiny 3, as fans continue to push for a continuation of the series. Bungie walked away from Destiny 2 earlier this year, with parent company Sony backing a focus on struggling extraction shooter Marathon instead. However, various Marathon updates have failed to kickstart the game, leading to ever louder calls for a return to Destiny. Despite the focal support for Destiny 3, it seems unlikely that Sony will green light the game, which would surely be yet another risky expensive development project at a time of extreme caution across the video game industry. But could Bungie have more Destiny in some shape or form in the works? With Marathon struggling for player numbers, how long will Sony give it before the axe falls on that game, too?

item.title: State of Play September 2026 has ended, and we have all the gameplay, trailers, and announcements from State of Play and State of Play Japan.
item.description: State of Play September 2026 ended with an extended look at Square Enix's Final Fantasy VII Revelation, but it was a broadcast dominated by no-shows and fan calls for Destiny 3. Highlights included an extended clip of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, the reveal of two new limited edition DualSense wireless controllers inspired by GTA 6, and the announcement of Crimson Desert DLC. We also got the surprise announcement of Maneater 2. Meanwhile, Until Dawn 2, Metro 2039, and Final Fantasy VII Revelation all got release dates. But there was disappointment at the various PlayStation Studios no-shows. For example, Sony Santa Monica's God of War Laufey, due out in February, was nowhere to be seen. Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet failed to make an appearance. And what's going on with Media Molecule, Sony Bend, and Haven's Fairgame? After State of Play ended, we rolled straight into State of Play Japan, where we got an extended look at Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara. Konami revealed two new games, and Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance got a deep dive.

item.title: Following the backlash to Rideshare Stimulator’s use of generative AI, developer Saber Interactive has reassured Warhammer 40,000 fans that the technology is not in Space Marine 3 in any way.
item.description: Following the backlash to Rideshare Stimulator’s use of generative AI, developer Saber Interactive has reassured Warhammer 40,000 fans that the technology is not in Space Marine 3 in any way. Fans of Space Marine 2 had expressed concern about the hotly-anticipated Space Marine 3 and AI when Saber confirmed generative AI had been used to develop Rideshare Stimulator, including speech and text in its Free Ride mode. Amid the controversy, Saber CEO Matthew Karch became embroiled in a public back-and-forth with former Rideshare Stimulator writer Stella Sacco, who stated that she had been "replaced" by ChatGPT after her departure from the project in 2023 — a claim Karch denied. "My PR team is always terrified by even broaching the subject but I would be happy to engage in a reasonable conversation about how AI can and should help shape gamer experiences," Karch told IGN at the time. "It's not and has never been about efficiencies and team reductions. Rather it's about how AI can improve the game experience.

item.title: Sony has dismissed calls to return some of the $500 million it will receive in tariff refunds, despite having already passed its extra costs onto consumers through console price rises.
item.description: Sony has dismissed calls from PS5 owners to return some of the $500 million it will receive in tariff refunds, despite having already passed its extra costs onto consumers through console price rises. The PlayStation maker has said it expects to recoup around half a billion dollars from the U.S. government, with the majority of this amount flowing back into its gaming division. Some PS5 owners say Sony should now return some of this windfall back to them, as the company has effectively now been paid twice — in the returned tariffs, and in the extra money it charged consumers following PS5 price rises, made during the era of tariffs to ensure it didn't lose its profit margins. Sony is far from the only company in this position, with Nintendo and Microsoft previously being pushed by fans to do the same. (Panic, the maker of indie handheld Playdate, has said it will do so, however.)

item.title: Andrew Garfield has admitted he's yet to congratulate Tom Holland on the incredible success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and still hasn't seen the movie.
item.description: Andrew Garfield has admitted he's yet to congratulate Tom Holland on the incredible success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and still hasn't seen the movie. Asked by Variety whether he had checked in with his fellow Spider-bro following Brand New Day's astonishing $2.3 billion box office bonanza, Garfield said he had not, and added that he didn't want his praise to be "disingenuous." "I don't want to be disingenuous," Garfield said. "A movie making money and people going to see it is an incredible thing, but I will reach out to him once I've seen the movie, which I'm very excited to see. And his other film, The Odyssey, I haven't managed to see either yet. I will send him a message when I see the work he has done." Hopefully the two blockbusters meet Garfield's expectations whenever he does get around to watching them.

item.title: Frontier Developments, the studio behind Jurassic World Evolution, Planet Zoo, and Planet Coaster, has inked a deal with Disney to develop an upcoming game.
item.description: Frontier Developments, the studio behind Jurassic World Evolution, Planet Zoo, and Planet Coaster, has inked a deal with Disney to develop an upcoming game. While details of the project remain thin on the ground for now, a press release sent to IGN stated that the game will "build upon the company's extensive experience and proven capabilities as a leader in the creative management simulation genre." In other words, expect a Disney sim game. It's not a huge leap to expect something akin to a Disneyland park creator, especially as the studio is well versed in extending its expertise to licensed properties via its Jurassic World Evolution franchise. Indeed, Frontier made 2011's Kinect: Disneyland Adventures, which was eventually remastered and made playable without Kinect. "We are delighted to announce this collaboration with Disney, which further reinforces our clearly defined strategy of developing and nurturing world-class creative management simulation game franchises," noted Frontier CEO Jo Cooke.

item.title: Zach Cregger admitted that he was “naive” to think his less-direct approach to adapting Resident Evil would be universally well-received by fans after deliberately choosing to avoid retelling the story exactly as it unfolds in the games.
item.description: Zach Cregger admitted that he was “naive” to think his less-direct approach to adapting Resident Evil would be universally well-received by fans after deliberately choosing to avoid retelling the story exactly as it unfolds in the games. Cregger’s Resident Evil movie follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who gets caught up in the madness of the Raccoon City Incident. The writer/director confirmed previously that this film takes place in parallel to the events of Resident Evil 2 and that it focuses more on what it feels like as a player to navigate through zombie-filled corridors and sneak around Lickers… but not everyone was anticipating an original story told within the continuity of Capcom’s beloved horror game franchise. Instead, a slew of fans have lashed out at Cregger for not directly adapting an existing game in the series, with many arguing that, without characters like Leon, Ada, and Jill, this isn’t really a Resident Evil movie at all. IGN’s Tom Jorgensen got the chance to sit down with Cregger to ask him about his feelings on this particular topic — and his response was strikingly self-aware.
